subject: Human Evolution
title: The Neanderthal Immune Boost
description: Learn The Neanderthal Immune Boost in one minute.

hook.text: When sapiens left Africa, they entered lands with unfamiliar pathogens. Neanderthals had lived there for ages.

buildup.text: Interbreeding gave sapiens Neanderthal immune genes already adapted to European and Asian diseases.

discovery.text: Toll-like receptor genes from Neanderthals boost innate immunity and still function in Eurasians today.

twist.text: The same inherited immune genes also increase risk of allergies—a side effect of a stronger response.

climax.text: Ancient interbreeding was an immunological shortcut: borrowing defenses that took millennia to develop.

punchline.text: Neanderthal genes still guard your health.

quiz.question: How did interbreeding with Neanderthals help Homo sapiens?
options: Sapiens gained immune genes adapted to Eurasian pathogens
